about: Every leak of a secret to a player's browser that a harness run has reproduced: what it is, which stage closes it, and where the harness sees it. A leak the audit lists that no run has reproduced is not here. Read by cluster.mjs (the check option knownLeak) and lib/canary.mjs (a hit an entry's match rules describe is that leak) and validated by node tools/check.mjs registry. An entry that stops reproducing fails its check, and so does an entry whose closing stage has shipped. D27: the killer's identity, the answer key, plans, GM notes, and anything critical or high may not be deferred; a metadata leak of medium or lower may be, as deferred: "1.3.x (D27)", described in README.md. A leak that gives the killer's identity may stand only as a foundryLimit, filed under the class killer-identity with its severity, never as metadata (DOC-02, 21.11.2026). From 1.3.0 only foundryLimit and deferred entries remain.

leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Token document, hidden or not, with its position, to every connected client; the owner chose on 03.11.2026 that an unfound trace stays a hidden token (D38 = 1), so where the traces lie is world data, while each trace's note and subject stay on the GMs' browsers.

leaks.what: Foundry's own secret doors (a wall of door type secret) are walls on every browser's map, with their type and state, so a player's console reads where they are; and a player's console can open one, which the primary GM's browser shuts again and sends a token that stepped through back. The module's secret passages are not such walls: Convert to passages turns these doors into them.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Scene's walls, with their door type and state, to every connected client, and lets a player change a door's state.

leaks.what: In a Class Trial the trial's list of the dead (trialProgress.mutedDead), a death nobody has found among them, is world data every player's browser holds, while nothing else of that browser's world says the student is dead. Public on purpose while the trial runs (the owner's TR30 = 2: the silenced microphone tells the table), taken out of the record when the trial ends.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 keeps a user's permissions, BROADCAST_AUDIO among them, in the user document every connected client holds; the owner chose that the trial mutes every ordinary dead student, a death nobody has found among them (TR30 = 2).

detectedBy.check: D2: no death nobody has found reaches a player's browser on the trial's list of the dead (TR30, E70-24)

leaks.what: A Monocub's purse (the Hope a Bribe, a Bounty or a Ghost Bet paid it) is the GMs' and its owner's, but its sheet's Hope and actions reach every browser: a move whose Hope price the purse paid lowers the actions and leaves the sheet's Hope where it was, so a console that watches the Monocub reads that its purse paid - that someone bribed it, a Bounty paid it or a bet came in. Who paid, and how much the purse holds, stay with the GMs and the owner.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Actor document, its resources among them, to every connected client; a purse kept on the sheet would show the purse itself.

detectedBy.check: A21b: a Monocub's move paid from its purse is read off its sheet - p3's copy of Botan shows no Hope go while the GMs' purse pays

leaks.classNote: Filed as metadata of severity info until 21.11.2026 (DOC-02): it resolves the "?" to the killer's name, so it is the killer's identity, a Foundry limit the module cannot close. The audit's reader of 1.2.118 records the owner's yes to this reading on 14.11.2026; this checkout holds no copy of that answer.
leaks.what: A killer behind a "?" after a murder's opening keeps their token document's actorId, so a player's browser console resolves the "?" to the killer's actor and name; the token's name, picture and flags, the cast copies and the module's packets name nobody, and nothing in the interface does. Since 1.2.116 the actor's own portrait wears the "?" too while its name stands (mask-gm.mjs writes its img), and another player's browser shuts that actor's sheet (anonymity.mjs `maskedSheetClosed`): the actor's name is world data a console reads all the same (read 21.11.2026; the audit's D-276).
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Token document to every connected client, and a token's actorId is what makes it that character's token: the module cannot point it at another actor without breaking the killer's own moves, sheet and rolls.

detectedBy.check: a masked token's actor is read from a player's console - on p2 and p3 the "?" token's actorId resolves to the killer's name

leaks.classNote: Filed as metadata of severity info until 21.11.2026 (DOC-02): it resolves the veiled tokens to the opening's killer, so it is the killer's identity. No owner's answer accepting it as a Foundry limit was found (nor by the audit's DOC-02); asked of the owner through the coordinator, 1.2.122.
leaks.what: While a direct murder's opening waits, the killer's tokens (and a third's on the killers' side) carry the veil's flag on every scene, so a player's browser console lists the flagged character tokens and resolves them by actorId to the opening's killer; since E112v the veil writes no Foundry hidden, so no character token turns hidden for it. The module's interface shows nothing - its voice tile neither counts nor names the killer for a player the veil hides them from since 1.2.119 (voice-tile.mjs personOf, R7864); what avclient-livekit's own window shows is LIVE-F119-03 - and the GMs' store of the veil does not reach a player.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Token document to every connected client, with its flags and its actorId, and the veil is the module's per-browser hiding: every browser that must not draw the killer's token has to be told which token it is, so what it reads a console reads (in the token's flags, a player's own cast copy or a packet alike; docs/dev/e112v/DESIGN.md section 3), and the killer's own browser reads the same flag to hold its microphone.

detectedBy.check: a veiled token's actor is read from a player's console - on p1 and p2 the tokens carrying the veil's flag resolve to the opening's killer

leaks.what: A barricaded room carries one region flag (movement.mjs ROOM_FLAGS.barricaded, drpgBarricaded) that every browser holds, so a player's console reads which rooms are barricaded. Who put the barricade up and how strong it is stay in the GMs' store barricades. Public on purpose: the owner's DA47.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Scene's regions with their flags to every connected client, and the walker's own browser has to read the barricade to refuse a walk in through its door (movement.mjs roomBarricaded, barricadedFrom); the owner chose the public flag for that (DA47, E74).

detectedBy.check: E74-A2: a barricaded room is read from a player's console - p2's browser reads the room's barricade flag while the barricade stands

leaks.what: A chat message a Spectator's own console forces past its browser's refusal is sent by Foundry's server to every browser before the primary GM's browser removes it (spectator-ui.mjs dropSpectatorMessage), so a console listening for createChatMessage on another player's browser reads its words for that moment. Nothing stays: no browser holds or draws it after the GMs have had it.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 gives a module no way to refuse a player's chat document before the server sends it to every connected client; the Spectator's own browser refuses it first (preCreateChatMessage, a courtesy a console steps past) and the primary GM deletes it on arrival.

detectedBy.check: chat2: a Spectator's message forced past its own browser is heard on p1's for a moment - p1's createChatMessage hook was handed its words before the GMs removed it

Before this, the scenario's own console road posted nothing headless (the shim's Hooks.events is a copy), so neither half had been read

leaks.classNote: Who hides and where their token stands, not who did anything: the hide is a player's own choice and names no crime. Low rather than info because it is the one thing the action promises to keep from the other players; put to the owner through the coordinator, 1.2.128.
leaks.what: While a character hides (Hide, an Infiltrate row), their tokens carry Hide's flag on every scene but the trial hall, so a player's browser console lists the flagged character tokens and resolves them by actorId to the hidden character, with the position every token document carries (foundry-hidden-tokens). The module's interface shows nothing: other players' browsers do not draw the token, their voice tiles neither count nor name the player, their pickers and Listen leave them out; the GMs' store of the hidden does not reach a player.
leaks.foundryLimit: Foundry v14 sends every Token document to every connected client, with its flags and its actorId, and the hide is the module's per-browser hiding, as the opening's veil is (foundry-veiled-token-actor): every browser that must not draw the token has to be told which token it is, and the hider's own browser reads the same flag to fade it and to hold its microphone.

detectedBy.check: a hiding token's actor is read from a player's console - on p2 the token carrying Hide's flag resolves to the hidden character
